one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban answers 'Who owns Benham Rise?' by explaining the legal rights the Philippines holds over this underwater plateau 250 km east of Northern Luzon with its 24-million-hectare area and 50-5,000m depth. UNCLOS -- signed December 10, 1982 in Jamaica and in force for the Philippines since November 16, 1994 -- established the four maritime zones measured from baselines defined by RA 9522 (approved by President Arroyo, upheld in Magallona v. Ermita, per J. Carpio, August 11, 2011): (1) 12-NM territorial sea (full sovereignty over air space, bed, and subsoil); (2) 24-NM contiguous zone (customs, immigration, and sanitary enforcement); (3) 200-NM EEZ (sovereign rights to explore and exploit all natural resources); (4) 350-NM continental shelf (exclusive exploitation rights, exclusive even if the Philippines does not yet explore). On April 12, 2012, the UN CLCS recognized the Philippines as an archipelagic state based on RA 9522's baselines -- a Cabinet member's 'We own Benham Rise now!' being 'a little exaggerated and legally inaccurate,' since the Philippines does not 'own' the seabed but holds incontestable exclusive maritime rights over it. China has publicly conceded these rights (even granting innocent passage), unlike its contested claims over the Spratlys and Scarborough. Even innocent passage can be temporarily suspended by the Philippines for security reasons or channeled through designated sea lanes. The column closes with the sidewalk analogy: the Philippines may not 'own' the adjacent sidewalk, but it has rights over it to protect security, health, and wellbeing.
